correctness.rationale: Coprimality permutes primitive roots and gives the integral reciprocal monic quotient of degree d(t−1). The formal kernel U_m/(1−X^m) gives W_{i,r} on blocks beginning at it, of length t except for the last length t−d+1. A vanishing period would force its nonzero prefix cyclotomic polynomial sum of degree <d to vanish at a primitive root, a contradiction. The first d−1 blocks thus contain support; the last contains the leading coefficient even if its Q=1 length is <m. The first supported position stays fixed and the last advances by m under any insertion of one period into a nonempty periodic prefix; the newly traversed gaps are exactly one cyclic histogram. These endpoint facts preserve each gap crossing a block boundary, proving the complete affine increment. In a gap wider than d the product of Φ_m with the low truncation of H has degree less than the far endpoint, so equals a nonzero prefix sum from Φ_m(X^t); evaluation at a primitive root again contradicts its minimal degree after undoing substitution. The initial coefficients at m−d and m are consecutive nonzeros for t>m, giving sharpness. The sum of all gap lengths equals the degree, yielding slope mass md. Independent exact division matched all eight slope vectors and all eight intercept vectors for m=15 and direct multiplication identity at one prime per residue class; their largest and second-largest distinct lengths match the Finding.
residual_risks: The independent finite certificate is for the displayed example, not a claim to replay the frozen 631-instance run. The affine identity requires Q≥1 and does not extend by this argument to Q=0.

evidence: The rival's proof uses only monic divisibility at primitive roots, the reciprocal kernel, a nonempty final block because it contains the leading coefficient, and the unconstrained period insertion lemma. No parity or squarefreeness is needed by any of those steps.
Zheng proves the maximum-gap bound and equality for the odd prime-extension cases in scope there, with multiplicities (for odd squarefree m and p>m, exactly 2 floor(p/m) maximum gaps).
broader_coverage.reasoning: All moduli are covered by the actual mechanism in the rival. Independently, writing R=rad(m), the standard identity Φ_m(X)=Φ_R(X^{m/R}) dilates every gap by m/R. If R=2s with s odd >1, Φ_{2s}(X)=Φ_s(−X) and coprime t is odd, so nonzero support is unchanged by the signs. On odd squarefree s dividing m, increasing t by m advances the prior cyclic increment m/s times. For m a power of two the quotient is (1+Y^t)/(1+Y), Y=X^{m/2} and t odd, giving the gaps directly. Thus the broader scope is mechanical even treating only the restricted theorem statement as a starting point.

Its m=15 table is exactly the one under review in a different normalization. The matching records are same-day: coverage and mechanical extension are established, chronological priority is not.
